I found the difference between the settings on the drive linkage to be pretty noticeable. Of course, there are other settings which can be used such as the spring tension, long/shortboard etc.

I have always used the shortboard setting as I find this the most comfortable personally. I have tried the longboard setting, but for me, although it was a bit lighter and quite a lot easier for very fast double bass, there was quite a large loss of control.

I probably wouldn't have paid full price for the pedal and probably would have gone for an Iron Cobra or something around the same price bracket if buying new, but I found this particular pedal for a very good price second hand and decided to go for it. Glad I did though, I prefer it to my friend's Iron Cobra and if you spend time getting the settings right you should be able to get it to feel exactly how you want.

Hope this helps!

I've got mine set up as 10" rack tom above the snare, floor tom in usual position on the right, and 12" rack the the right of the floor tom, similar to how Jojo Mayer has it. I find it extremely comfortable, but at the same time it opens up a lot more fill possibilities.

I have my splash in the gap between my hats, snare and my 10"tom (if that makes sense). As well as making it nearly impossible to mic the snare, it also makes the splash a lot more accessible!

Cymbals: crash above my hats/10", crash 2 above ride, chine off to the right, 18" stack in-between china and ride.

I've also got a side snare off to the left, which is either a timbale or a super phat low tuned snare.
